title: The Vaccine That Gave Polio to 40,000 Children
hook: In 1955, a faulty polio vaccine batch paralyzed 40,000 kids—and the government covered it up for decades.
why_this_can_go_viral: Uses a well-known medical milestone to reveal a hidden tragedy, leveraging outrage and shock.

title: The Doctor Who Buried Patients Alive—to 'Study' Death
hook: A 19th-century physician buried people alive to study the process of dying, with their full consent—or so he claimed.
why_this_can_go_viral: Extreme, visceral imagery and a taboo subject create irresistible curiosity and shock value.

title: The FDA-Approved Drug That Caused Organ Failure in 14 Days
hook: An FDA-approved diabetes drug caused liver failure in patients within two weeks—and stayed on the market for two years.
why_this_can_go_viral: Targets distrust in regulatory agencies and taps into fear of prescribed medications.

title: The Disease Cover-Up: They Knew the Paint Gave Kids Lead Poisoning in 1900
hook: Lead paint manufacturers knew it poisoned children in 1900—but fought to keep it on walls for 78 more years.
why_this_can_go_viral: Reveals a century-long corporate conspiracy that still affects millions, fueling righteous anger.

title: The Doctor Who Removed 1,000 Healthy Gallbladders for Profit
hook: A surgeon in Pennsylvania removed healthy gallbladders from over 1,000 patients—earning millions before a whistleblower stopped him.
why_this_can_go_viral: Extreme betrayal of trust and high patient count evoke visceral disgust and personal vulnerability.

title: The Pharmaceutical Giant That Sold Cough Syrup with Heroin
hook: Bayer sold heroin as a 'non-addictive' cough syrup for children in the 1890s—and called it 'Bayer Heroin.'
why_this_can_go_viral: Shocking name recognition and historical irony drive shares and comments.

title: The Experiment Where Doctors Gave Children Radioactive Breakfast Cereal
hook: In the 1950s, doctors fed radioactive oatmeal to children with intellectual disabilities—to study digestion.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines vulnerable victims with radioactive betrayal, sparking deep empathy and outrage.

title: The FDA-Approved Anti-Nausea Drug That Caused Limb Deformities
hook: An FDA-approved anti-nausea drug caused thousands of babies to be born without limbs—but stayed legal in America.
why_this_can_go_viral: Iconic medical tragedy with ongoing relevance; triggers protective instincts and anger at regulators.

title: The Hospital That Harvested Organs from Patients With Do-Not-Resuscitate Orders
hook: A California hospital harvested organs from patients who had DNR orders—before they were legally dead.
why_this_can_go_viral: Fear of bodily autonomy violation and moral horror drive high engagement.

title: The Skincare Company That Sold 'Anti-Aging Cream' with Mercury
hook: A best-selling anti-aging cream contained mercury at levels 2,000 times the safe limit—turning users' skin gray and toxic.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines vanity with hidden poison, creating a strong cautionary tale for beauty users.

title: The Disease Cover-Up: They Knew the Air Fresheners Caused Asthma in Babies
hook: Manufacturers of plug-in air fresheners knew their chemicals triggered severe asthma in infants—but called them 'fresh scent.'
why_this_can_go_viral: Relatable household product reveals hidden danger, forcing viewers to question everyday items.

title: The Doctor Who Used Radiation on Pregnant Women—'For Science'
hook: A Chicago radiologist X-rayed pregnant women's bellies weekly for 10 years, tracking the damage to their unborn children.
why_this_can_go_viral: Innocence of unborn children and prolonged betrayal evoke maximum emotional response.

title: The Pharmaceutical Company That Sold 'Allergy Medicine' with Cocaine
hook: Cocaine was a legal ingredient in allergy drops for 30 years—and the company marketed it to children as 'toothache drops.'
why_this_can_go_viral: Shock factor of cocaine in children's medicine and historical irony create shareable content.

title: The Hospital That Refused to Call 911 When a Patient Stopped Breathing
hook: A Philadelphia hospital had a policy: if a patient collapses, don't call 911—let them die to save money.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exploits fear of being abandoned in a hospital; pure systemic horror drives shares.

title: The Supplement Brand That Sold 'Weight Loss Pills' with Tapeworm Eggs
hook: A 1920s supplement company sold pills containing live tapeworm eggs—promising 'eat anything and stay thin.'
why_this_can_go_viral: Gross-out factor and historical absurdity make it highly shareable and memorable.

title: The Doctor Who 'Cured' Cancer with a $20,000 Machine That Did Nothing
hook: A doctor sold a 'frequency machine' to cancer patients for $20,000—it was just a light bulb with a speaker.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exploits desperation of cancer patients; outrage and pity create strong emotion loop.

title: The Disease Cover-Up: They Knew the Mattress Flame Retardants Caused Cancer
hook: Chemical companies knew flame retardants in children's mattresses caused cancer—but fought for decades to keep them legal.
why_this_can_go_viral: Every parent sleeps on a mattress; personal relevance and hidden danger drive engagement.

title: The Experiment Where Doctors Gave Syphilis to Prisoners—Without Telling Them
hook: In the 1960s, doctors injected syphilis into prisoners to test a new antibiotic—and let the disease progress for months.
why_this_can_go_viral: Mimics notorious Tuskegee study in a new setting; evokes sharp moral outrage.

title: The Hospital That Hid a Mafia Body Disposal Ring in the Morgue
hook: A Detroit hospital morgue was used by the mafia to dispose of murder victims—and the staff helped for 20 years.
why_this_can_go_viral: Crime cross-over with healthcare setting creates unique, shareable shock narrative.

title: The Skincare Brand That Sold 'Whitening Cream' with Liquid Mercury
hook: A global whitening cream brand contained liquid mercury at toxic levels—causing kidney failure in users across three continents.
why_this_can_go_viral: Global scope and beauty vanity trap create cross-cultural outrage and discussion.

title: The Doctor Who Faked Cancer Diagnoses—to Sell Chemotherapy
hook: A Michigan oncologist diagnosed 600 patients with cancer—only 1 had it. The rest were injected with chemo for profit.
why_this_can_go_viral: Ultimate betrayal of trust; combines false hope, poison, and profit in the highest-stakes medical horror.
